InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.title: Belyi maps, dessins d'enfants, and three-point covers, Part II: inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.reason: Start from Belyi's existing combinatorial, analytic, algebraic and arithmetic contracts. Retain the general scheme-theoretic fundamental group and its comparison with Belyi's field-theoretic carrier, arithmetic specialization, rational rigidity, solvable realizations and Hurwitz spaces. The introduction must list BelyiMaps first among prerequisites, respect its named staged successors, and distinguish source specifications from declarations available at the programme pin.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.keeps: The finite-étale Galois-category instance for the connected schemes in the selected SGA range, its geometric fibre functor, and the induced scheme-theoretic fundamental group using Mathlib's existing automorphism-group topology and classification equivalence. Establish the finite-étale connected-component interpretation and ordinary geometric-basepoint comparison, including the existence and choice dependence of fibre-functor isomorphisms. Recover π₁(Spec K) from ModularCurves 0D's field-case equivalence, and prove the characteristic-zero algebraically closed G_m computation with its Tate-twist/choice convention. Compare the three-punctured-line scheme carrier with Belyi 12.5–12.6's field-theoretic group by an equivalence compatible with geometric fibre functors. Arithmetic path-torsor objects and tangential points remain NC.0's extension of these interfaces.
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.reason: The abstract Galois-category classification and profinite Aut(F) are already in pinned Mathlib. Belyi explicitly excludes the scheme-theoretic carrier and its comparison, so its special case does not discharge the general scheme target. ModularCurves already owns the finite-étale field equivalence; the Spec K acceptance theorem is an application of it.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.keeps: The geometric/arithmetic exact sequence for geometrically connected schemes under the selected SGA hypotheses; scheme-theoretic decomposition/inertia embeddings and their conjugacy dependence; tame quotient and wild-inertia behaviour in that scheme setting; and specialization maps for smooth proper families with the precise characteristic and prime-to-p restrictions. Prove compatibility with Belyi's existing three-punctured-line exact sequence and peripheral inertia through IG.0's comparison. Import finite function-field ramification from AlgebraicCurves and the local-field statements only under their finite-residue-field hypotheses. Retain the finite-field Frobenius and punctured-curve acceptance instances and the nonvanishing of wild inertia before passing to a tame quotient.
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.reason: Belyi 12.8–12.9 owns the three-point field-theoretic sequence and inertia; AlgebraicCurves 8 and LocalFieldsRamification own their distinct arithmetic ramification settings. None supplies the full general scheme sequence or the smooth-proper specialization theorem. In particular, finite-residue-field tame theory cannot be silently applied at a geometric characteristic-zero puncture.

Hilbert irreducibility over number fields, full-group specialization away from the branch locus, simultaneous avoidance and linearly disjoint specializations, with infinitely many distinct worked extensions and their certificates, are beyond Belyi's programme and remain here.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.keeps: Branched-cover realization from generating product-one tuples for general finite branch sets, its comparison with the imported three-point construction, braid/Hurwitz actions on the relevant Nielsen classes, and general cover descent beyond the Belyi-pair case. Prove a source-qualified rational rigidity criterion, distinguishing generation, inner versus absolute equivalence, centralizers and rationality of conjugacy classes; import the product-one and generating-triple counts for the three-point case. Keep a worked rigid arithmetic realization and an actual example where the field of moduli is not a field of definition. Keep the dessin/triple and branch-cycle/ramification acceptance checks as applications of Belyi's comparison, including a passport that does not determine the pair. Import the Belyi carriers, theorem, analytic/algebraic comparison, field-of-definition certificates and positive descent results without reproving them.
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.reason: IG.3 already says it consumes the three-point programme; explicit supplier edges make that handoff enforceable. Belyi excludes arbitrary branch sets and Hurwitz spaces. Its 11.6 records the negative moduli/definition phenomenon only as a warning and constructs no counterexample, so IG.3 must keep the requested constructed example. A product-one count or a one-element passport is not by itself rational rigidity.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.keeps: Arithmetic finite embedding problems on the profinite supplier's existing carrier and weak-solution notion; the properness condition as surjectivity of that same continuous lift; local constraints and compatibility with restriction to local Galois groups. Retain the selected proof of Shafarevich's solvable realization theorem, including the abelian-kernel steps, auxiliary ramification and successive proper solutions; cyclic and dihedral realizations and the test that a weak nonsurjective solution is insufficient.
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.reason: ProfiniteProPGroups 5.1 owns the generic finite embedding problem and weak solution, but explicitly does not assert proper solutions. The arithmetic proper-solution theorem and its local hypotheses remain IG.4, not a renamed generic lifting theorem.

Hurwitz moduli, braid/Nielsen-class components, descent and regular-extension interfaces remain. Preserve tame positive-characteristic covers with p prime to the group order, the characteristic-zero/tame-reduction example, and the wild patching/Abhyankar realization proof subtasks. Reuse IG.3 and the existing algebraic-moduli input. Belyi explicitly excludes Hurwitz spaces and arbitrary branch sets; LPV.5 is a specialized monodromy application, not an established supplier of all this material.

InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.keeps: Export actual polynomials, extensions, cover maps and Galois-group isomorphisms with the specialization hypotheses supplied by IG.2–IG.5. Import the explicit symmetric-group family from PolynomialGaloisGroups rather than reproducing it. Transport Belyi's arithmetic action, field-of-moduli/definition distinction, cyclotomic branch-cycle convention and source-scoped faithfulness along the earlier comparison maps; do not rebuild those actions or prove a stronger faithfulness theorem. Export the IG fundamental-group interfaces to NC.0 and reference NC.0's arithmetic path-torsor construction when packaging the final interface, without constructing a second torsor. Preserve the theorem-indexed solved-family list, and mark the unrestricted inverse Galois problem over Q and generic-polynomial universality as frontier statements, never proved inputs.
InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGro.reason: This is an application and interface layer. Belyi owns its actions and faithfulness, PolynomialGaloisGroups owns its explicit S_n realization route, and NC.0 owns arithmetic path torsors. The supplier direction for those torsors is NC.0 → IG.6; NC.0 consumes IG.0/IG.1, not IG.6, so no cycle is introduced.
